scope: Proposition 4.1 (Moment and rank conversion) of the manuscript “Compatibility entropy and the spectrum of a Thorp sweep” (preprints/Compatibility-entropy-and-the-spectrum-of-a-Thorp-sweep-September-26-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dae8f5ca5b99fbec), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 18. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose, for p > 0 and 0 < ε ≤ 1/2, that X ρ̸=1 Dρ Tr |Bρ|p ≤ ε. (20) Then every nontrivial ρ and every 1 ≤ r ≤ Dρ satisfy sr(Bρ) ≤ ε Dρr !1/p . (21) The full regular singular list, with its constant value at index 1, satisfies sj(B) ≤ j−1/p (1 ≤ j ≤ |G|). (22) For every integer M with 2M ≥ p, M independent convolution steps have worst-start total- variation distance at most 1 2 √ ε from uniform. Conversely, if sj(B) ≤ j−c for an absolute c > 0 over a family of finite groups and their convolution operators, then for each fixed ε > 0 there is a fixed p′ > 0, independent of the group, for which (20) holds with p′ in place of p.
